title: Pages
lead: Create independent working drafts, publish reviewed snapshots and compose layouts from typed public data.

sections.title: Create a page and choose its content format
steps: Open Pages → New page. Enter a title, for example “Our services”, and choose a generic model when a starting structure is useful. Duplication is a separate action in Overview.

JSON and HTML/Mustache are synchronized views of one document. Edit html in JSON or use the visual/code editor; bindings and the original structured content are preserved. Invalid JSON blocks switching and saving without discarding the buffer.
Use Save draft. The immutable page ID remains stable when its URL changes; a working draft does not replace an existing published snapshot.

sections.title: Write and format the body
steps: Write direct plugin references in HTML/code. The Core resolves them automatically; existing saved bindings remain compatible.
In HTML/Mustache, use the shared Visual editor for text, headings, lists and links. Use Code for semantic HTML and protected dynamic structures; switch back to inspect the result.
Use Preview to review the current composition in the active template. Preview is private; it does not publish the page.

Describe the service and its intended audience.

sections.title: Insert public images and videos
steps: Upload new files in Images first. The editor’s repository selector only selects existing files; public pages cannot select private media.
Use the image or video tool and open the local media selector. Search, sort, switch list/grid view and paginate; choose the desired public file. Alternatively, enter a permitted remote URL.
Provide useful image alternative text and review the result. Global Settings defines the public/private repository roots. Remote links receive rel protections including noopener and noreferrer.

sections.title: Set structure, metadata and sharing defaults
steps: In Publication, enter the editorial author and mark Pending review when the working draft needs review. This name is editorial text, not an administrator login. Explicit publication releases the reviewed snapshot.
Open the properties panel. In Structure and address, set the URL and parent page; use stable IDs for relationships. Example: place “Consulting” under “Our services”.
Set a featured image and alternative text, then write a concise Summary. These values can be reused by listings and social metadata.

Open SEO and behavior for title, description, canonical, indexing and social overrides. Leave optional overrides empty to retain inherited editorial/global defaults. Advanced options contain model and native document controls.

Set Order in the editor and sort the flat catalog by its Order heading or request pages:records/children with sort order. Choose Page template from the active theme layouts compatible with the current native content. This does not change the global theme.

sections.title: Bind data from other plugins
steps: In HTML/Mustache, choose an enabled plugin service, fill its typed parameters and add a unique alias. For example, bind blog:posts as news with limit 3.
Insert the loop below in Code. Variables are escaped data; the receiving HTML/template defines structure and appearance. Use # for lists/sections and ^ for an empty state.
Write direct plugin references in HTML/code. The Core resolves them automatically; existing saved bindings remain compatible.

sections.title: Publish, schedule and manage the catalog
steps: Save pending edits before publishing. The UTC publication date can be backdated; a future date schedules release. Publish and Schedule use the same date control. Pending review is never a public state.
Open Overview to search, filter, sort or paginate pages. Edit or duplicate a page from its actions. Configure the page size in Pages → Settings.
Unpublish a page when it should leave the public site. Home and 404 remain protected. A public URL never exposes an unpublished working draft.

sections.title: Recover pages and revisions
steps: Open History to inspect available revisions before restoring one. Restoration produces a working draft for review.
Move a removable page to Trash, which is the last sidebar item. Open Trash to recover it as a draft and review its content before publishing.
If another edit changes the revision, reload and reconcile changes. Revision conflicts prevent silent replacement; do not discard an unsaved buffer without reviewing it.

sections.title: Reuse Pages data in other layouts
steps: Bind pages:records for a paginated listing; set limit, page, sort and direction. Bind pages:details, pages:children or pages:breadcrumbs with an immutable id for a single page, direct children or ancestors.

Use item fields id, title, summary, url, image.url, image.alt, parentId, author, order, createdAt, updatedAt and isCurrent. Author/order come from the published snapshot, not unsaved or private working metadata. The older pages:list service remains available with title, text, href and image.

For example, bind pages:records as directory, limit 6, page 1, sort title, direction asc and render the loop below. Homepage can also use a published Page as a document source without duplicating the site frame.

sections.title: Direct plugin data and template positions
body: Use pages.<id-or-slug> for one page and pages.latest.limit.20.page.2.items for a paginated collection. Publication time controls descending order; the global content page size caps each page. Item data includes title, summary, url, author, image and literal content. Body strings are escaped and never evaluated as nested templates.
steps: Use the stable identifier or slug without dots. Explicit id.<value> and slug.<value> selectors disambiguate reserved names.
Place named query parameters before field paths; use sections (#) and inverted sections (^) for finite iteration and empty states.
Keep presentation in the receiving layout. Template positions require manifest declarations and source-plugin assignments.

sections.title: Edit one document through JSON or HTML
body: The JSON document contains html, bindings and content. html is the canonical editorial source in both tabs; content preserves native fields and is not a second rendering source. Existing native pages receive portable semantic HTML on opening, with no storage changes until an explicit save. Native Slides blocks and existing component markers remain live source references, without saving rendered plugin output. Unsupported custom block types require an explicit authored layout.
steps: Switch to JSON to edit the html string or preserved data. Valid JSON updates the HTML editor; HTML and visual edits update the same JSON document.
Correct invalid JSON before switching or saving. The invalid buffer remains available and cannot overwrite saved content.
Save a draft, reopen either tab and inspect the same content. Publish only after saving; the public page uses the saved html while Mustache resolves at request time.

sections.title: Search, sort and paginate the overview
body: The overview uses shared CMS table controls. Search and status/type filters are at the top; Clear resets filters. Click a column heading to select ascending or descending order; the active arrow identifies the current ordering.
steps: Use the icon controls and their translated tooltips. Search, clear and ordering restart at page one; page navigation preserves the selected filters and order.

All result rows and the seven-position pager scroll together with the page. The pager follows the complete table or grid without covering any result; only wide tables scroll horizontally. Ellipsis buttons open upward menus containing earlier or later pages outside the three displayed numbers. Use the keyboard or a page button to navigate.
Read the total results, displayed range/count and page totals below the pager. Unavailable directions and empty catalogs retain disabled controls.

Every page is an independent row. Parent identifies its relationship; click a parent name to filter its direct children. Parent relationships and the Order field remain available in creation/editing; there is no tree-view toggle.
